channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: Carney’s speech: The rupture is a necessary part of the transition
item.description: Mark Carney’s Davos warning about a global “rupture” frames Canada’s turn toward China and America’s accelerating imperial decline as the “suddenly” after decades of gradual erosion.

item.title: Print preserves more truth; social media destroys it
item.description: A biology professor recalls exposing a racist hoax via print encyclopedias and argues that today’s unregulated internet lets such falsehoods spread and erode trust in science.

item.title: You Decide: Can the beat go on for North Carolina?
item.description: North Carolina’s booming, record-setting economy is drawing jobs and investment, but rising costs, congestion and loss of open space raise doubts about how long the growth can last.

item.title: Church news: Congregations gather for weekly services
item.description: Upcoming worship services, special events and church news submission details for Wilson-area congregations.

item.title: Parent charged with assaulting school officials
item.description: Wilson parent Tomeka Nicole Eatmon is charged with assaulting two staff members during a disturbance at Jones Elementary School and remains jailed on $5,000 bond ahead of a Feb. 23 court date.

item.title: 2 men charged with attempted murder
item.description: Two Wilson men are jailed without bond on attempted murder and first-degree kidnapping charges after police say they seriously assaulted a 47-year-old man they knew in a targeted attack.

item.title: Grants help local groups offer arts projects
item.description: Wilson Arts has awarded $28,203 in Grassroots Arts Subgrants for 2025–26, backing local festivals, theater, youth programs, photography, music and community art projects across Wilson County.

item.title: Chamber celebrates community leaders
item.description: At the Wilson Chamber of Commerce’s 102nd annual meeting, 3C Store Fixtures owner Carolyn Daniel was named Distinguished Citizen, while Grant Goings and Jack Wiggins received lifetime membership honors.

item.title: County under state of emergency as storm approaches
item.description: Wilson County has declared a state of emergency ahead of a winter storm expected to bring significant ice, power outages and closings from Saturday night through Monday.

item.title: NCHSAA Basketball Glance, Jan. 23, 2026
item.description: Farmville Central boys and Kinston girls lead Eastern Plains, while Northern Nash, Rocky Mount, SW Edgecombe and Wilson Prep headline NCHSAA conference races in the Jan. 23 basketball glance and Friday matchups.
